title: iCloud, OneDrive and Google Drive: syncing and sharing

videos.script: Three services, one idea, and the idea is worth more than the differences between them. {{idea}} A synced folder is a folder that is also on a server, and also on every other device signed in to the same account. You change a file, the change is uploaded, the server pushes it to everything else. That is the whole mechanism and it runs about once a second. {{mech}} Which produces two things people find surprising. The first is that deleting a file deletes it everywhere within seconds, including from the laptop that is closed in somebody else's bag. {{del}} The second is that two devices editing the same file while one of them is offline is a situation with no correct answer, and each of the three services guesses differently. {{conflict}} So this lesson is the mechanism, the conflict, what each service actually does, and where the space goes. {{plan}} And it finishes on the sentence from lesson eight, which has not stopped being true: this is not a backup, and the reason is in the first paragraph.
